pharm: Active R-enantiomer of cetirizine; non-sedating peripheral H1 blocker
summary: Levocetirizine is the active R-enantiomer of cetirizine, a second-generation H1 antihistamine providing relief from allergic rhinitis and chronic idiopathic urticaria at a lower dose than racemic cetirizine. Standard adult dose is 5 mg once daily in the evening, taken with or without food. It undergoes minimal hepatic metabolism and is largely excreted renally, so dose reduction is required in renal impairment and it is contraindicated in ESRD or hemodialysis. It is among the less sedating antihistamines but can still cause somnolence; alcohol and other CNS depressants should be avoided.
indications: Relief of symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis
Relief of symptoms of perennial allergic rhinitis

dosage.n: Less severe cases: 2.5 mg once daily may suffice; max 5 mg/24h

admin: Administer orally once daily, preferably in the evening
May be taken with or without food
Do not exceed the recommended dose
Children 6–11y with any degree of renal impairment should not receive levocetirizine
moa: Levocetirizine is the active R-enantiomer of cetirizine and acts as a selective, peripheral histamine H1 receptor antagonist. By competitively blocking H1 receptors it inhibits the effects of histamine released during allergic responses, reducing rhinorrhea, sneezing, pruritus, and wheal-and-flare reactions. It penetrates the CNS poorly, limiting sedation relative to first-generation antihistamines.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to levocetirizine, cetirizine, or hydroxyzine
relative: Predisposition to urinary retention or bladder outlet obstruction

preg: Limited human data; former FDA category B. Use only if clearly needed.
lact: Levocetirizine/cetirizine expected to be present in breast milk; not recommended, use with caution.
renal: Dose adjustment required. CrCl 50–80: 2.5 mg once daily; CrCl 30–50: 2.5 mg every other day; CrCl 10–30: 2.5 mg twice weekly. Contraindicated in ESRD (CrCl <10) and hemodialysis. Not for use in children 6–11y with any renal impairment.
hepatic: No dose adjustment for isolated hepatic impairment. Adjust dose in combined hepatic and renal impairment based on renal function.

interactions.diagnostics: Discontinue approximately 3 days before allergy skin testing (suppresses wheal-and-flare response)

monitoring: Renal function (especially when dose adjustment is needed)
counsel: Take the dose in the evening
Avoid alcohol and other sedating medications
May cause drowsiness — use caution when driving or operating machinery
Do not exceed the recommended dose
Stop the antihistamine about 3 days before allergy skin testing
pk: ~8–9 h (longer in renal impairment; ~6 h in children)
pearls: Active R-enantiomer of cetirizine — achieves the same effect at a lower dose
Among the least sedating second-generation antihistamines but more sedating than fexofenadine
Minimal hepatic metabolism; eliminated mostly by renal excretion
missed: Take when remembered; if near the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Somnolence in adults; agitation followed by drowsiness in children. No specific antidote; provide supportive care. Not effectively removed by dialysis.
